questions.q: Why is a star schema called that?
options: A single fact table sits at the center, with its denormalized dimension tables radiating outward as the points of the star
It requires exactly five dimension tables, arranged like a star's points
Star schemas can only be used for astronomy data
It refers to the star rating of the warehouse's query performance
questions.explain: Every dimension in a star schema connects directly to the central fact table, one join away, forming the classic star shape.

questions.q: What actually happens in a snowflake schema?
options: One or more dimensions are normalized into multiple related tables instead of one flat table
The fact table is split into several smaller fact tables
Dimension and fact tables are combined into a single table type
All numeric measures are converted into dimension attributes
questions.explain: A snowflake schema doesn't change the fact/dimension classification — it normalizes one dimension (e.g. Product) into related tables like Product, Subcategory, and Category.

questions.q: What's the main query-performance cost of snowflaking a dimension?
options: More joins are required to reach the fully described dimension data, compared to one join in a star schema
Snowflaked dimensions cannot be joined to fact tables at all
Snowflaking always doubles the fact table's row count
There is no performance cost — snowflaking is always faster
questions.explain: Because a snowflaked dimension is split across multiple related tables, reaching the full hierarchy requires one join per normalized level, instead of the single join a denormalized star dimension needs.

questions.q: According to Microsoft's own dimensional modeling guidance, what is the default recommendation for dimension tables?
options: Dimension tables should almost always be denormalized (star); snowflaking is the exception, not the starting point
All dimensions must always be snowflaked for correctness
Dimensions should never contain more than two columns
There is no default recommendation either way
questions.explain: Microsoft's guidance treats denormalized star dimensions as the default, reserving snowflaking for specific cases like very large dimensions or the need to relate higher-grain facts to a hierarchy level.

questions.q: Which is a legitimate, Microsoft-cited reason to snowflake a dimension anyway?
options: You need keys that relate the dimension to a higher-grain fact table, such as a sales-target table stored at the subcategory level
Snowflaking is required whenever a dimension has more than one attribute
Fact tables cannot join to denormalized dimensions
Snowflaking is purely a stylistic preference with no design justification
questions.explain: One concrete case for snowflaking is needing a key at a coarser grain level of the hierarchy (e.g. subcategory) so a higher-grain fact table can join to exactly that level.
